t: That such conveyance shall contain the further provision that if the Alaska Council of Boy Scouts of America shall at any time cease to use the property so conveyed for recreation and other public purposes title thereto shall revert to the United States.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that naming an outside nonprofit (the Alaska Council of Boy Scouts of America) and "public purposes" signals outside involvement. But this is only a reverter condition in a land conveyance: title returns to the United States if the grantee stops using the land for the stated purposes. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: if the Alaska Council of Boy Scouts of America shall at any time cease to use the property so conveyed for recreation and other public purposes title thereto shall revert to the United States

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a condition subsequent for a land conveyance, specifically a reversionary clause. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from the Boy Scouts or any other outside party before making a decision. The interaction described is a legal consequence of non-compliance with land use terms, not a participatory process in decision-making.
qwen_block.s: That such conveyance shall contain the further provision that if the Alaska Council of Boy Scouts of America shall at any time cease to use the property so conveyed for recreation and other public purposes title thereto shall revert to the United States.

opus.w: This clause is a reversion condition in a land conveyance. It does not set up consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body or a right to sue. A non-federal organization is named, but only as the party receiving the property. It has no role in shaping any federal decision, so this is like receiving a benefit, not participating.
opus.s: if the Alaska Council of Boy Scouts of America shall at any time cease to use the property so conveyed for recreation and other public purposes title thereto shall revert to the United States

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a condition on a property conveyance where title reverts to the United States if the Boy Scouts cease using the property for public purposes. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The mention of 'public purposes' refers to the nature of the land use, not a participatory process involving the public in federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: That such conveyance shall contain the further provision that if the Alaska Council of Boy Scouts of America shall at any time cease to use the property so conveyed for recreation and other public purposes title thereto shall revert to the United States.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "public purposes" implies public participation or access. However, the definition of participation requires the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties *before* making a decision. This section describes a condition on a property conveyance (a deed restriction) where title reverts to the US if the Boy Scouts stop using it for public purposes. It does not establish a process for the public or any outside entity to participate in a federal decision-making process. The Boy Scouts are the grantee, not a participant in a federal decision via consultation or advisory role. The "public purposes" clause is a standard reverter clause, not a mechanism for public input into federal policy or decisions.
